description.narrative: Construction of Makambako-Songea transmission line and distribution lines to provide sustained access to reliable and affordable electricity within six districts in the Iringa and Ruvuma regions of Southern Tanzania (Ref 71002060 credit part)

Konstruktion av Makambako-Songea transmission och distributions-linjer för tillgång till hållbar, tillförlig elektricitet till överkomligt pris inom sex distrikt i regionerna Iringa och Ruvuma i södra Tanzania.

The major objective of the project was to extend TANESCOs electricity network in order to provide electricity to commercial business activities, fresh water pumping, secondary schools, medical services, streetlights, residential houses, etc. within the project area. The project aimed to provide and improve supply of electricity to economic centers, social and welfare utilities and households in rural villages, peri-urban areas and towns in Njombe and Ruvuma regions in Tanzania.

sector.narrative: Electric power transmission and distribution (centralised grids)

description.narrative:
The agreement between the Governments of Tanzania and Sweden for this project was signed in 2008, with Sweden committing approximately 700 million SEK, equivalent to TZS 165 billion by then, for the construction of the transmission line and rural electrification. The project has successfully connected around 100,000 people in 23,232 households across 120 villages to the electricity distribution network. The final report confirms that 100% of these households now have electricity. Seeing these results, we can confidently say that the investment has been well spent.
During the ceremony of official closing of the project the Ambassador of Sweden in Tanzania Charlotta OzakMasiac congratulated the Government of Tanzania through the Ministry of Energy, the Ministry of Finance, TANESCO, and REA, as well as the contractors and consultants, as well as other who have worked tirelessly to deliver this project, and Tanzania and Sweden should be proud of the achievement.
Beyond electrification, this project has enabled TANESCO to decommission diesel power stations in Songea, Mbinga, Namtumbo, and Ludewa. This not only results in significant cost savings for the Government but also reduces air pollution, both from the generators themselves and from the transportation of diesel from Dar es Salaam. This is a major step toward a cleaner energy sector, contributing to environmental sustainability and greenhouse gas reduction.
Assessing the results against the projects objectives, allocated funds, and overall scope, we are proud to conclude that the Makambako-Songea Project has successfully achieved its intended goals, despite challenges and delays. The project has made significant contributions to social and economic development across the region. The available data highlights that the results have benefited all segments of the community, including women and men, urban and rural populations, children and adults, and people from diverse economic backgrounds.
On the economic front, the project has facilitated growth of local businesses, stimulated trade, and created new employment opportunities, supporting the regions long-term economic resilience. Access to reliable electricity has empowered small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to expand their operations, while larger industries have gained improved stability and efficiency.
Socially, the electrification of healthcare facilities has enhanced the quality of medical services, ensuring better maternal care, emergency services, and vaccine storage. Educational institutions now benefit from reliable power, enabling evening classes, digital learning, and improved facilities, creating better opportunities for children and young adults.
The project's success reflects a meaningful reduction in inequalities, bridging the gap between urban centers and rural areas, and promoting sustainable, inclusive development that will continue to benefit the community for years to come.
